text:
Jacob Stein: Hey @Marcus Lin - could you take a look at the incident-bot redaction + audit logging plan before we widen the beta? We’re about to flip on restricted-mode posting + config diff collector. PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/incident-bot/pull/0125 (config diff redaction), https://github.com/redwood-inference/incident-bot/pull/0128 (restricted mode). We want a security signoff + any must-do changes.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Current behavior: bot posts “context bundle” to incident thread in #incidents unless restricted flag is set for the incident, then it posts minimal summary in #incidents and full bundle to a restricted channel allowlist. Biggest open Q is auditability for what got redacted + what was posted.

Marcus Lin: :eyes: skimming now. Quick take: direction is good, but we need a few hard requirements before broad rollout.

Marcus Lin: Main concerns:
1) “Safe to post” logic can’t be heuristic-only. Needs default-deny + allowlist for config keys and fields.
2) We need an audit trail of bot output (at least hashes + metadata), not just “we tried to redact”.
3) Prevent accidental leakage via URLs and headers (query params, signed URLs, bearer tokens) and via JSON blobs in logs.

Sean Gallagher: Re (1) we have an allowlist for config diff keys currently (routing_policy.*, feature_flags.*) + explicit denylist for keys w/ “token|secret|key|auth|cookie”. But agree heuristic-only is risky.

Marcus Lin: Denylist by substring isn’t enough. You’ll miss things like `x-amz-security-token` / `sig` / `X-Slack-Signature` / `Authorization` / `api_key` in nested dicts.

Jacob Stein: What would you want? More aggressive redaction patterns?

Marcus Lin: Concrete asks:
- Use a structured “redaction policy” file with:
  a) allowed paths (exact match + glob)
  b) denied paths (exact match + glob)
  c) value redactors (regexes for common secret formats)
  d) max field length + truncation rules
- Require each collector to emit a `classification` per field: `SAFE`, `REDACTED`, `OMITTED`, `UNKNOWN`.
- If any field is `UNKNOWN`, default behavior should be OMIT (or at least keep it out of #incidents).

Benji Okafor: On config snapshots: we can give you stable paths for effective config so the allowlist can be strict. E.g. `routing.routes[*].match`, `routing.routes[*].target_model`, `routing.routes[*].fallbacks`, `limits.rpm`, `limits.tpm`, `autoscaling.min_replicas/max_replicas`.

Aisha Bello: Also from on-call POV: if you omit unknown fields, please show a line like “N fields omitted due to classification=UNKNOWN. Use /incident-bot full in restricted channel” so responders know it’s intentional.

Marcus Lin: Yep. Transparency without leaking.

Rafael Mendes: For audit trail, we were thinking: log the posted bundle to our internal event stream w/ incident_id, collector versions, and the rendered Slack blocks. But security-wise should we store full content or only digests?

Marcus Lin: Prefer:
- Store full content ONLY in restricted storage (access-controlled) with short retention (e.g. 14 days) for debugging.
- For general audit, store metadata + hashes:
  - incident_id
  - channel posted to
  - posting mode (normal vs restricted)
  - bundle_id
  - per-collector: name, version/git sha, start/end time, status
  - hash of (pre-redaction payload) and hash of (post-redaction payload)
  - counts: fields_redacted, fields_omitted

Marcus Lin: You need a way to prove after the fact what got posted without keeping sensitive raw values around forever.

Jacob Stein: Makes sense. We can implement an “audit event” emitted by the bot on every post.

Sean Gallagher: What about Slack itself? It’ll contain the message history. If we post full bundle in restricted channels, that’s still retention per Slack policy.

Marcus Lin: That’s why channel allowlist + restricted channel membership needs to be tight. Also, for the restricted channel message, please avoid including anything that can be construed as customer content. E.g. no request bodies, no prompts, no customer org names. Even if “restricted”, we should minimize.

Rafael Mendes: Totally. Bundles should be operational metadata only.

Marcus Lin: Specific leak vectors I saw in PR 0125 examples:
- Config diff showing `headers_to_add` (could include auth headers)
- Routing policy containing `webhook_url` / callback URLs (often include secrets in query params)
- “Change links” to CI logs can include signed URLs

Benji Okafor: `headers_to_add` we can classify as forbidden entirely. For webhook URLs, we can allow the host + path but strip query params.

Jacob Stein: We already have a URL sanitizer in the Slack formatter that does `?…` -> `?[redacted]` if query present. But it’s not applied everywhere.

Marcus Lin: It must be applied everywhere you render a URL. Also watch for JSON-encoded URLs inside strings.

Marcus Lin: Requested changes before broad rollout:
1) Central redaction library used by all collectors + formatter (no custom per-collector regex).
2) Add tests with fixtures that include:
   - bearer tokens, JWTs
   - AWS keys
   - Slack tokens
   - URLs with `sig=`, `token=`, `X-Amz-Signature=`, etc.
   - headers/cookies
   - base64-ish blobs (cap at length, redact if matches token-ish patterns)
3) Add “restricted-mode enforced” switch: if incident is marked customer-sensitive, bot MUST NOT post any bundle sections to #incidents beyond minimal metadata.

Sean Gallagher: What’s “minimal metadata” in your view?

Marcus Lin: In #incidents:
- incident id, service, region(s), severity, start time
- links to dashboards/runbook (no customer identifiers)
- statement: “Full context posted in restricted channel #incidents-restricted (or whatever), request access via on-call manager”
No deploy commit titles if they include customer names (rare, but it happens). Keep deploy info minimal.

Aisha Bello: +1 on deploy commit titles. We’ve had “hotfix for CustomerX” in commit messages. :grimacing:

Jacob Stein: Good catch. Our deploy collector currently includes PR title + author. We can change to PR number + repo + short SHA and keep title behind restricted mode only (and sanitize even there).

Rafael Mendes: We can also strip anything after first 80 chars and run the same sanitizer.

Marcus Lin: Please treat PR titles as untrusted input. I’d prefer not posting titles at all by default.

Jacob Stein: OK. We’ll adjust deploy collector format.

Marcus Lin: Also need an approval workflow for adding new allowlisted config keys. E.g. CODEOWNERS on the redaction policy file includes eng-security.

Benji Okafor: That’s fine. We can put it under `incident-bot/redaction/policy.yaml` and add CODEOWNERS for it.

Jacob Stein: Draft of policy file could look like:
```yaml
version: 1
posting:
  public_channels:
    allow:
      - "#incidents"
  restricted_channels:
    allow:
      - "#incidents-restricted"
paths:
  allow:
    - "deploys[*].service"
    - "deploys[*].region"
    - "deploys[*].commit_sha"
    - "deploys[*].pr_number"
    - "config_diff.routing.routes[*].target_model"
    - "config_diff.limits.*"
    - "saturation.gpu.queue_depth"
    - "saturation.gpu.utilization"
  deny:
    - "**.headers*"
    - "**.authorization*"
    - "**.cookie*"
    - "**.webhook_url"
value_redactors:
  - name: "jwt"
    regex: "eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+"
    replacement: "[redacted:jwt]"
  - name: "bearer"
    regex: "(?i)bearer\\s+[A-Za-z0-9._-]{16,}"
    replacement: "[redacted:bearer]"
  - name: "url_query"
    regex: "(https?://[^\\s?#]+)(\\?[^\\s#]+)"
    replacement: "$1?[redacted]"
limits:
  max_string_len: 200
  max_list_items: 20
```
We’ll keep it simple but centralized.

Marcus Lin: This is close. A few tweaks:
- `deny` needs to win over `allow` always.
- Add redaction for email addresses and IPs (customer identifiers sometimes show up in config/comments).
- Add explicit rule to drop anything called `notes`, `description`, `comment` fields (free text is dangerous).

Sean Gallagher: Noted. We can drop any “freeform” strings by default.

Rafael Mendes: For audit logs, we’ll emit an event like:
`incident_bot.bundle_posted` with fields: incident_id, mode, posted_channels, bundle_hash, redaction_policy_version, collector_statuses, omitted_fields_count, redacted_fields_count.

Marcus Lin: Works. Also log “who invoked” for manual requests (e.g. `/incident-bot more`). If it’s automatic post, mark as `trigger=auto`.

Jacob Stein: Ack.

incident-bot: (system) Reminder: please avoid pasting tokens or customer payloads in this channel.

Aisha Bello: One more: for config diffs, we should show “key changed” without showing values sometimes. Like for `routing.routes[*].match` maybe OK, but for any field that could include customer IDs, show `changed (value omitted)`.

Marcus Lin: Exactly. “Diff summary” mode is safer:
- show changed paths + counts
- only show values for allowlisted “safe scalars” (numbers, enums)

Benji Okafor: That’s doable. Most risky fields are strings.

Jacob Stein: We’ll implement `diff_render_mode` per path: `values`, `type_only`, `presence_only`.

Marcus Lin: Nice. Make sure it’s in the policy file and covered by tests.

Sean Gallagher: Timeline-wise, what’s the gate for rollout? We were aiming to widen next week.

Marcus Lin: Gate items for me:
- Central policy file + CODEOWNERS
- Default deny / omit unknown
- PR titles removed from public posting
- Audit event emitted for every post + manual request
- Fixture tests for secrets + URL sanitizer applied everywhere
If those land, I’m OK with expanding beta to more on-call rotations.

Rafael Mendes: Cool. We’ll add these as blocking tasks in Linear (ENG-2847 / ENG-2845 area) and ping you for re-review.

Jacob Stein: Thanks Marcus. I’ll push updates and re-request review on PR 0125/0128 once the policy + audit event wiring is in.

Marcus Lin: :thumbsup: tag me when ready. Also loop in @Aisha Bello to sanity check “omit/unknown” messaging so responders don’t assume bot is broken.

Aisha Bello: Will do.
